reason: This passage focuses primarily on relationships between nobility—Saul (king), Jonathan (prince), and David (anointed future king). The few 'regular people' who appear in the narrative are portrayed neutrally or functionally without positive characterization. Jonathan's young servant merely follows orders without being characterized. David's family and the people at Saul's table are mentioned only briefly and not portrayed with particular favor. The strong favorable portrayals—courage, loyalty, righteousness, honor—are exclusively reserved for Jonathan and David, who are members of the royal and anointed classes, not regular people.
